stories: God speaks the universe into being in six days, makes people in His own image, and rests on the seventh day.
God forms Adam from the dust, plants a garden for him, and makes Eve as his partner.
The serpent tempts Eve, Adam and Eve disobey God, and they are sent out of Eden, but God promises that evil will one day be crushed.
Jealous of his brother, Cain kills Abel, and God confronts him.
God saves Noah, his family and the animals in the ark, and sets the rainbow as a sign of His promise.
Proud people try to build a tower to the heavens, and God scatters them with many languages.
God tells Abram to leave his home and promises to bless all nations through him.
To keep the peace, Abram lets his nephew Lot choose the best land.
God promises Abram descendants as many as the stars, and Abram believes Him.
Hagar runs away into the desert, and the God who sees meets her there.
The Lord visits Abraham and promises that Sarah will have a son, and Sarah laughs.
Abraham pleads for the city, and God rescues Lot before judgment falls.
God keeps His promise: Sarah has a son in her old age.
God tests Abraham's faith and provides a ram in place of his son.
Abraham's servant prays for guidance and meets Rebekah at the well.
Hungry Esau trades his birthright to his brother Jacob for a bowl of stew.
Jacob disguises himself to receive his father's blessing meant for Esau.
Running for his life, Jacob dreams of a stairway to heaven and God's promise.
Jacob works seven years for Rachel, but is tricked into marrying Leah first.
Jacob wrestles all night, receives a blessing, and is renamed Israel.
Esau runs to meet Jacob and embraces him: the brothers are reconciled.
Joseph's jealous brothers sell him as a slave and tell their father he is dead.
Joseph refuses temptation, is falsely accused, and lands in prison, but the Lord is with him.
Joseph explains the dreams of Pharaoh's cupbearer and baker.
Joseph interprets Pharaoh's dreams of famine and becomes ruler over Egypt.
Famine drives Joseph's brothers to Egypt, where they bow before the brother they sold.
Joseph reveals who he is and forgives his brothers: what they meant for evil, God meant for good.
A mother hides her baby in a basket on the Nile, and Pharaoh's daughter finds him.
Moses kills an Egyptian, flees to Midian, and God hears His people's cry.
God speaks to Moses from a burning bush and sends him to free Israel.
Pharaoh hardens his heart as God sends plague after plague on Egypt.
The blood of a lamb protects Israel's homes, and Israel leaves Egypt that night.
God parts the sea for Israel and saves them from Pharaoh's army.
God feeds His hungry people in the desert with manna and quail.
When the people are thirsty, God brings water out of a rock.
On Mount Sinai, God gives His people the Ten Commandments.
While Moses is on the mountain, the people make an idol, and Moses pleads for them.
Ten spies spread fear, but Joshua and Caleb trust that God will give them the land.
Bitten people who look at the bronze serpent are healed.
A prophet's donkey sees the angel of the Lord before he does.
Rahab hides Israel's spies in Jericho because she believes in their God.
The river stops flowing so Israel can cross into the promised land.
Israel marches around Jericho, shouts, and the walls fall down.
The prophet Deborah leads Israel to victory over Sisera's army.
God calls fearful Gideon and defeats Midian with just three hundred men.
Samson loses his strength through Delilah, then calls on God one last time.
Widowed Ruth refuses to leave her mother-in-law: your people will be my people.
Boaz shows kindness to Ruth and redeems her; their great-grandson is King David.
Hannah pours out her heart to God for a son and gives Samuel back to the Lord.
The boy Samuel hears God calling in the night: speak, for your servant is listening.
Searching for lost donkeys, Saul finds Samuel and is anointed king.
God chooses the youngest shepherd boy: the Lord looks at the heart.
A shepherd boy with a sling and faith in God defeats the giant.
Saul's son Jonathan protects his friend David from his father's anger.
David has the chance to kill King Saul in a cave but refuses.
Abigail's courage and wisdom stop David from taking revenge.
King David welcomes Jonathan's disabled son to eat at his table.
David brings the ark of God to Jerusalem with joy.
David sins, the prophet Nathan confronts him, and David repents.
David's son rebels against him, and David weeps over his death.
Solomon asks God for wisdom and settles the case of two mothers and one baby.
God's glory fills the temple as Solomon prays for his people.
A queen travels far to test Solomon's wisdom and praises his God.
Rehoboam's harsh answer splits Israel into two kingdoms.
Ravens feed Elijah, a widow's flour never runs out, and her son is raised to life.
Elijah challenges the prophets of Baal, and God answers with fire.
Worn out and afraid, Elijah meets God in a gentle whisper.
King Ahab and Jezebel steal a vineyard, and Elijah announces God's judgment.
A chariot of fire takes Elijah, and Elisha receives his spirit.
A woman who welcomed Elisha sees her son brought back to life.
A foreign army commander washes seven times in the Jordan and is healed.
A young king rediscovers God's law and leads the nation back to God.
Babylon destroys Jerusalem and the temple, and the people go into exile.
Isaiah sees God's holiness and answers: here am I, send me.
God shows Jeremiah a potter reshaping clay: like clay in His hand.
God breathes life into dry bones, a picture of hope for His people.
Jonah runs from God, is swallowed by a great fish, and learns about God's mercy.
Daniel and his friends stay faithful to God in the king's palace.
Three young men refuse to bow to an idol and are kept safe in the fire.
A mysterious hand writes on the wall, and Daniel reads its message.
Daniel keeps praying, and God shuts the lions' mouths.
A Jewish orphan is chosen as queen of Persia.
For Such a Time as This
Esther risks her life to go to the king and save her people.
Esther exposes Haman's plan, and her people are saved.
Nehemiah prays, asks the king, and leads the rebuilding of Jerusalem.
Job loses everything but still refuses to curse God.
Job meets God, humbles himself, and is restored.
An old priest is told he will have a son, John the Baptist.
Gabriel tells Mary she will be the mother of the Son of God.
Elizabeth's baby leaps for joy, and Mary sings praise to God.
Jesus is born in Bethlehem, and angels announce the good news to shepherds.
Two faithful old people recognise the baby Jesus as the promised Saviour.
Wise men follow a star to worship the newborn King.
Joseph takes Mary and Jesus to Egypt to escape King Herod.
The Boy Jesus at the Temple
At twelve, Jesus amazes the teachers in His Father's house.
As Jesus is baptized, a voice from heaven says: this is my beloved Son.
Jesus answers each of the devil's temptations with God's word.
After a miraculous catch of fish, Peter and his partners leave everything to follow Jesus.
At a wedding in Cana, Jesus performs His first sign.
Jesus tells a religious leader he must be born again: for God so loved the world.
Jesus offers living water to a Samaritan woman, and her whole town believes.
Jesus teaches who is truly blessed, and calls His followers salt and light.
Friends lower a paralyzed man through a roof, and Jesus forgives and heals him.
Jesus speaks to the wind and the waves, and they obey Him.
A sick woman touches Jesus' cloak, and a little girl is raised to life.
A boy's five loaves and two fish feed a huge crowd.
Peter steps out of the boat and walks toward Jesus on the water.
Jesus shines with glory on a mountain, with Moses and Elijah.
Jesus gives sight to a man born blind: I was blind, but now I see.
Martha is busy serving, while Mary sits and listens at Jesus' feet.
Jesus weeps with His friends, then calls Lazarus out of the tomb.
A tax collector climbs a tree to see Jesus, and his life is changed.
A blind beggar calls out to Jesus and receives his sight.
Jesus welcomes little children: the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.
A rich man asks how to have eternal life but walks away sad.
A poor widow gives two small coins: more than all the others.
Mary pours costly perfume on Jesus' feet in an act of love.
Seed falls on different kinds of soil, like God's word in different hearts.
The Mustard Seed and the Yeast
God's kingdom starts small but grows great.
One house is built on rock, the other on sand.
An unlikely stranger shows what it means to love your neighbour.
A man stores up riches for himself but is not rich toward God.
The Lost Sheep and the Lost Coin
Heaven rejoices over one sinner who repents.
A runaway son comes home, and his father runs to welcome him.
The Pharisee and the Tax Collector
God hears the humble prayer: God, be merciful to me, a sinner.
A forgiven man refuses to forgive another: how often should we forgive?
Five are ready when the bridegroom comes, and five are not.
Servants are trusted with their master's money: what will they do with it?
Whatever you did for the least of these, you did for me.

section: The Cross and the Empty Tomb
stories: Jesus rides into Jerusalem on a donkey as crowds shout Hosanna.
Jesus drives out the money changers: My house will be a house of prayer.
The Lord and Teacher kneels to serve His friends.
Jesus shares bread and wine: my body given for you, my blood poured out.
Jesus prays in agony, not my will but yours, and is arrested.
Peter denies knowing Jesus three times, then weeps bitterly.
The Roman governor finds no fault in Jesus but hands Him over to be crucified.
Jesus is crucified, forgives His enemies, and gives up His spirit.
Joseph of Arimathea lays Jesus in a tomb, and guards seal the stone.
The women find the tomb empty: He is not here; He has risen!
Weeping at the tomb, Mary hears the risen Jesus call her name.
Two disciples walk with a stranger and recognise Jesus as He breaks bread.
Thomas sees the risen Jesus: my Lord and my God!
The risen Jesus cooks breakfast and restores Peter: do you love me?
Jesus promises the Holy Spirit and is taken up to heaven.
The Holy Spirit comes like fire, Peter preaches, and three thousand believe.
Peter and John heal a lame man in the name of Jesus.
Stephen sees Jesus in heaven and forgives those who stone him.
Philip explains Isaiah to an Ethiopian official, who is baptized.
Saul on the Road to Damascus
A bright light stops Saul, the persecutor, and he becomes a follower of Jesus.
God shows Peter that the good news is for every nation.
An angel leads Peter out of prison while the church prays.
Paul and Silas sing at midnight, an earthquake opens the doors, and the jailer believes.
Paul tells the philosophers of Athens about the unknown God.
Paul's ship is wrecked in a storm, but everyone reaches land safely.
A New Heaven and a New Earth
God makes all things new and wipes away every tear.
